I look around the cottage. Morning light's coming through the window. Ainsley's up, folding blankets. The children are still sleeping, or pretending to.

I reach for my coat, the one with the patched elbow.

"Ainsley." She looks up. "Taking the deep shaft today. The shallow one's not paying out."

That's all I say about it. That's all I'll say.

I need to get moving. The ore outcrop's where I earn, and earning's what I need to do. Marta's loan sits in my chest like a stone. Five weeks of thin seam I've kept to myself. Today I dig deeper, or I find another way.

I walk to the door. My tools wait in the shed. I'll eat when I come back, if I hold anything worth bringing back. </think> I'm at the outcrop now. Morning mist still clings to the rocks. The shallow seam I've been working—you can see it from here, the water running out pale as dishwater. No copper in that water. Hasn't been for weeks.

The deep shaft is half a mile east. Longer walk, shorter daylight, more risk if the ceiling's unstable. But a seam that's running thin doesn't fill a debt.

I set down my pack and look at the outcrop proper. Copper ore mined here, that's what the place is for. I could try the shallow seam one more time, or I could work what the outcrop offers directly.

My hands know the pick. My eyes know the water. The shallow seam's done being kind to me.

I'll mine what I can from the outcrop itself today, and tomorrow I'll take the deep shaft if this doesn't pay. </think>  I swing the pick down, and the strike comes back wrong. The ore's there—one unit, small enough to fit in my hand—but the feel of it tells me what I already knew. This outcrop's thinning out too.

I pocket the copper ore. One unit. That's one unit closer to 400 sim, if I can find a buyer. Or if I can work it into something worth more than raw ore.

The sun's higher now. I've got hours yet before the light fails on the deep shaft. I could mine again—try for more of this thin stuff—or I could walk the copper to someone who might buy it, or I could head home and face Ainsley's eyes knowing I've brought back barely enough to mention.

I'll mine once more. Give this outcrop a fair chance to surprise me.  </think> The second strike comes up bare rock at first, then a seam no wider than my thumb. I work it careful, not to collapse what little's left. Two units now. Two units of copper ore in my pack.

I sit on a stone and look at the gap in the rock where I took the second piece. Water seeps out, pale-green, barely any copper in it at all. The color of water running out empty.

I could stay and swing until I'm chasing dust. Or I could take what I have and find who's buying.

Marta bakes at her shop. She might take ore in trade, though owing her already puts a taste in my mouth. Better to sell direct, get the sim in hand, not owe more than I do.

I stand up. Two units. Not the 400 I need. Not enough to even look at yet. But it's something.

I'll head to town. See who's at the market, who's buying what I hold. Marta's shop is there, but maybe there's another buyer. Anyone else.

The deep shaft waits for tomorrow. Today, I see what two lumps of rock can buy me.  2,910 sim remaining. 

I walk back toward town. The sun's warm on my back. The debt walks ahead of me, patient, not saying a word. I know it's there. That's enough talking for one morning.
